translation.title: Easter Island's South Coast and Anakena Beach
translation.lead: Explore Ahu Vaihu and Akahanga, the Rano Raraku quarry, Tongariki's fifteen moai and Anakena Beach in a single day.
included: Private excursion with an English-speaking guide.
notes: A Russian-speaking guide is available for an additional charge.

hero.hover: Moai on the grassy slope of the Rano Raraku quarry — illustration

translation.body:
The journey begins along the island's southern coast. See the unrestored platform at Ahu Vaihu in Hanga Tee Bay and Ahu Akahanga, where, according to tradition, King Hotu Matu'a is buried.

Next comes Rano Raraku, the quarry where most of the island's moai were carved. Hundreds of statues still lie or stand on the slopes of the extinct volcano. The figures associated with this stop are 900 moai and 397 statues remaining in the quarry area. A packed lunch is included outdoors.

Continue to Ahu Tongariki, the island's largest platform, with fifteen restored moai. The route then leads to Ahu Te Pito Kura and the stone known as the 'Navel of the World'.

At Anakena Beach, white sand and palm trees sit beside the Ahu Nau Nau platform. There is time for a walk and a swim before returning through the island's interior to Hanga Roa and your hotel.
